input: Research electric vehicle tax credits and rebates

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: EV incentives exist at federal, state, and local utility levels — knowing which levels to cover determines the breadth and depth of research needed.
Eligibility rules differ sharply for individual consumers vs. businesses or fleets, and income thresholds or filing status can affect which credits apply.
The specific vehicle being considered (new, used, make/model, battery size) directly determines which credits it qualifies for under current law.
Geographic location (state/country) is a hard constraint that determines which state rebates, utility programs, and local incentives are even relevant.
Whether the user needs a quick summary, a detailed breakdown, or a comparison table affects how the research should be formatted and delivered.
Knowing whether the goal is to make a purchase decision, file taxes accurately, or simply learn the landscape defines what 'done well' looks like.
Some users want only the largest or most accessible incentives; others want every possible credit listed — this shapes how exhaustive and prioritized the research should be.

gold.taskTitle: Research EV tax credits and rebates
gold.taskDescription: Find and compile relevant electric vehicle tax credit and rebate information to support a purchase or financial decision.

questions.title: Which incentive levels should be covered — federal, state, local, or all?
questions.description: Determine whether the research should focus on federal credits only (e.g., IRS Form 8936), state-level rebates, local utility programs, or a full multi-level overview.

questions.title: Is this for a personal purchase or a business fleet?
questions.description: Identify whether the buyer is an individual taxpayer or a business entity, as commercial EV credits have different rules and caps than consumer credits.

questions.title: Do you have a specific vehicle make, model, or type in mind?
questions.description: Pinpoint whether a particular new EV, used EV, or plug-in hybrid is being considered, since credit eligibility is tied to the vehicle's MSRP, battery capacity, and assembly origin.

questions.title: What state or country are you located in?
questions.description: Establish the geographic location to filter for applicable state rebates, local utility incentives, and regional programs that are irrelevant outside that area.

questions.title: What format do you want the findings delivered in?
questions.description: Clarify whether the user needs a concise summary, a detailed written report, a comparison table, or talking points — this shapes how the research is structured.

questions.title: What decision is this research ultimately meant to support?
questions.description: Determine whether the end goal is choosing when and what to buy, preparing a tax return, comparing total cost of ownership, or general financial awareness.

questions.title: Should every possible incentive be listed or only the highest-value ones?
questions.description: Establish whether the user wants an exhaustive, every-dollar-counts list or a prioritized view of only the most impactful and accessible credits and rebates.
